subtopics.title: Sorting the Moves — A Vocabulary for Migration

questions.question: A daily commuter is NOT a migrant because:
options: Commuting is too cheap to count
Migration requires a permanent or semi-permanent change of residence, and a commuter returns home

questions.question: A person who leaves Zimbabwe and settles in South Africa is called:
options: An emigrant from Zimbabwe and an immigrant into South Africa

questions.question: A refugee differs from an internally displaced person because a refugee:
options: Has crossed an international border fleeing persecution or conflict

questions.question: Mineworkers spending eleven months on the mines and each December at home, year after year, illustrate:

subtopics.title: Push and Pull — Why People Move

questions.question: Push factors are:
options: The costs of the journey between two places
The permits needed at a border
The negatives of the place of origin that drive people out

questions.question: Which family of factors dominates world migration?
options: Economic factors — most migrants move toward work and wages

questions.question: Chain migration means:
options: Existing migrant communities at the destination make each next migration easier, strengthening the stream
Migration only happens along railway lines

questions.question: People keep migrating into cities that already have severe unemployment because:
options: They are forced to move there by law
They move on a perceived picture of the destination that is often brighter than its reality

subtopics.title: Case Study — Rural Eastern Cape to Gauteng

questions.question: The historical roots of the Eastern Cape to Gauteng stream lie in:
options: The discovery of diamonds in the Eastern Cape
A government resettlement programme of the 1990s
The province's position on the coast
The homeland system and the migrant labour system, which confined families to poor land while men worked mine contracts

questions.question: A decisive pull factor lowering obstacles for new Eastern Cape migrants to Gauteng is:
options: Relatives and home-community networks already established there

questions.question: For the rural origin areas, the migration stream causes:
options: Overcrowding of village schools by working adults
Remittances and returning skills as gains, but the loss of working-age adults, leaving children and grandparents

questions.question: For Gauteng as destination, the stream brings:
options: A young workforce and larger economy, but informal settlement growth and overcrowded services

subtopics.title: Case Study — Crossing Borders into South Africa

questions.question: The main causes of the Zimbabwean migration stream to South Africa from around 2000 were:
options: Economic collapse with hyperinflation and unemployment, compounded by political fear

questions.question: The Zimbabwean stream is called mixed migration because it contains:
options: Voluntary economic migrants, refugees and asylum seekers, and everything between

questions.question: For origin countries such as Zimbabwe, emigration to South Africa brings:
options: Remittances as a lifeline, but a brain drain of teachers, nurses and skilled workers
The return of all skilled workers
An end to unemployment at home

questions.question: The xenophobic violence of 2008 and 2015 is explained in the lesson as igniting where:
options: Border posts process the most permits
Competition for scarce jobs, housing and services concentrates in the poorest areas

questions.question: The two sorting questions for any migrant's story are:
options: Did they cross a border, and did they choose to move

questions.question: The same journey earns a person two labels — emigrant and immigrant — because:
options: Each label depends on which side of the border is speaking
One label is for documents, the other for the census

questions.question: The two-place life of the historical mine contract system meant:
options: Mineworkers settled permanently at the mines with their families
Families moved to the mines every December
Eleven months in a mine hostel and December at home, repeated for years — oscillating between two homes

questions.question: In the tug-of-war picture, the knots in the rope stand for:
options: The pull factors of the city
Obstacles between origin and destination — fares, distance, borders and leaving family

questions.question: Every cousin already in Johannesburg makes the rope pull harder because:
options: Cousins pay for all expenses forever
Family ahead means a place to sleep and someone who knows where jobs are — so each mover recruits the next

questions.question: Which pairing correctly matches a push with its mirror pull?
options: Failing farm at home — jobs and wages in the city
War at home — drought in the city
Good school at home — no school in the city
Peace at home — persecution in the city

questions.question: For many rural households in origin areas, remittances are:
options: A small bonus at year end
The main income — groceries, school shoes and electricity

questions.question: The both are true at once point about origin villages is that they:
options: Gain remittance money while losing their working-age adults

questions.question: The four boxes answer pattern for migration consequences covers:
options: Origin gains, origin losses, destination gains, destination strains

questions.question: The destination city's gains from migration include:
options: Young, determined workers — nurses, builders, shopkeepers — whose labour and businesses build the economy
